items.title: BYD names geopolitics as biggest hurdle, puts US passenger car sales on hold
items.summary: SINGAPORE: The number one challenge to expansion for BYD is geopolitics, Stella Li, BYD's executive vice president, said on Thursday, months after the Chinese company's chairman said it aims to become the world's largest automaker within five years. Li said the company has decided to not sell passenger cars in the US for now despite being in the US for "a long time" as it is "complicated." Li said BYD has no plans to partner with other Chinese companies given its leadership in various areas such as storage and solar panels.

items.title: Vietnam busts ring accused of stealing 2,700 cats for slaughter
items.summary: HANOI: Police in Vietnam have arrested 12 people accused of stealing 2,700 cats and selling them for slaughter in Ho Chi Minh City, the Ministry of Public Security said this week. Investigators said he also bought live cats and resold them to customers seeking cat meat To supply the operation, Binh allegedly worked with several accomplices who recruited younger people to capture cats in residential neighbourhoods. Police said he also supplied traps used in the thefts The group operated mainly between 11pm and 4am, using fish bait and traps placed outside homes with pet cats.

items.title: Who holds the gavel? COP31's unusual Australia-Türkiye deal
items.summary: AUSTRALIA and Turkiye are co-hosting the 31th United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) next month but the highly-unusual decision to share leadership has raised questions about how the climate summit will unfold —and who holds the power. Both countries had fought to host the high-profile event, forcing a compromise under which Turkiye would stage COP31 but Australia would run the formal negotiations. Australia's Climate Change and Energy Minister Chris Bowen was named "president of negotiations" and granted "exclusive authority" of the negotiations.

items.title: Nearly 300,000 Nepalis at flood risk: Study
items.summary: NEW DELHI: More than 1,400 people were killed and 5,000 remain missing after catastrophic floods hit Nepal in August – and a new study Thursday warned nearly 300,000 people face similar risks. The disaster raised fears that similar floods could strike elsewhere as glaciers retreat and development expands across fragile mountain terrain. "Our results demonstrate rapidly increasing exposure in Himalayan catchments," key study scientist C. Scott Watson, from Britain's University of Leeds, told AFP.

items.title: War shakes Netanyahu's support in Israel's north
items.summary: On Israel's border with Lebanon where Hizbollah fired thousands of rockets and drones, previous backers of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu say they are rethinking how they will vote in the first election since the war. "Many I know were right-wing and were Bibi supporters, and today they're not," said plant nursery owner Sigal Malachi, using a nickname for Israel's longest-serving premier. In traditional strongholds of Netanyahu support, many said they could no longer back his right-wing government in the Oct 27 vote, accusing it of failing to secure a lasting quiet with the resistance fighters.

items.title: Indonesia arrests three ferry executives over deadly Java Sea sinking
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesian police have arrested three executives of the company that owned a passenger ferry that sank in the Java Sea last month, killing dozens of people, a spokesman said Thursday. The Indonesian suspects, who worked for the shipping company that owned and operated the ferry, stand accused of negligence, national police spokesperson Trunoyudo Wisnu Andiko said in a statement. Police arrested the ferry's captain last month.

items.title: Haze: 36 areas record unhealthy API readings, Seremban and Segamat highest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Haze conditions remained concerning tonight, with 36 areas nationwide recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10pm. According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Seremban in Negri Sembilan and Segamat in Johor recorded the highest API reading at 188. They were followed by Nilai, Negri Sembilan (184); Bukit Rambai, Melaka (178); Kluang, Johor (178); Bandaraya Melaka (177); Tangkak, Johor (177); and Johan Setia, Selangor (177).

items.title: 'Stunned' Madrid mourns pensioner who sparked housing protests
items.summary: MADRID: One of hundreds of housing protesters camping in central Madrid, Aitana Lopez felt duty-bound to pay tribute to a pensioner whose eviction sparked a movement that culminated in early elections. The death of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal on Wednesday drove a "stunned" Lopez to lay a candle on Thursday at an improvised shrine in the Spanish capital's Puerta del Sol square, the epicentre of the protests. Abascal, who used a wheelchair, died in hospital two weeks after her eviction from the Madrid apartment where she had lived for 70 years.

items.title: NST Leader: Stop treating government loans like grants
items.summary: The government is making viability assessments mandatory before any new federal loans are approved. We are talking public money being disbursed as federal loans here. Ministries or agencies extending loans must clearly distinguish between commercial projects and projects serving a public or social obligation.

items.title: Motorcyclist, pedestrian injured in viral Lebuh Chulia crash
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A motorcyclist was injured and a pedestrian suffered a fractured leg after a crash on Lebuh Chulia on Oct 5. Northeast deputy police chief Superintendent Lee Swee Sake said police detected a 46-second video of the incident circulating on WhatsApp today. Lee said the motorcyclist sustained minor injuries, while the pedestrian suffered serious injuries, including a fractured leg, and was still receiving treatment in hospital.

items.title: ICC says Philippine ex-president Duterte fit to be tried
items.summary: THE HAGUE: Former Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte is fit to stand trial on charges of committing crimes against humanity during a crackdown on the drug trade, the International Criminal Court said Thursday. Duterte had the capacity to "understand the charges, understand the purpose and consequences of the proceedings, follow the course of the proceedings," said the experts, quoted in the court ruling. The tribunal prosecutes individuals for the world's worst crimes such as war crimes and crimes against humanity.

items.title: Haze: Schools in four states, KL, Putrajaya and Rompin to close
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Schools in four states, including one district in Pahang, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya will be closed tomorrow following the worsening haze situation. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the closures involve all schools in Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as schools in Rompin, Pahang. Fadhlina urged parents to continue following official updates from their respective schools, district education offices and state Education Departments.

items.title: Attack risks rise for tankers as Iran vows to block more Hormuz routes
items.summary: LONDON: Tankers are facing a higher risk of attacks and intimidation as they try to get critical shipments through the Strait of Hormuz after Iran issued new warnings it would block routes that it has not authorised, sources said. Iran has now warned regional countries that any attempt to open new routes for oil exports would be considered hostile, a senior regional official close to Teheran told Reuters. In recent months, Gulf oil producers have rushed shipments of oil through channels that hug the Omani side of the strait before transferring the oil in open waters in the Gulf of Oman with aerial support from the US, sources have told Reuters.

items.title: Dozens protest in Tokyo after Marine accused of murder in Okinawa
items.summary: TOKYO: Dozens of protesters lined up in front of Japan's Foreign Ministry on Thursday after a US Marine was accused of killing a woman in the southernmost prefecture of Okinawa, many holding signs decrying crimes by US service members. The case is the latest in a string of incidents stretching back years that have fuelled unease over the large US troop presence on the island chain near Taiwan and China, with US officials warning it could undermine ties vital to security in East Asia. Japan hosts the largest overseas contingent of US forces globally.

items.title: Anwar extends condolences over deaths of three siblings in Pontian crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed his condolences over the deaths of three siblings killed in a road crash in Pontian, Johor, today. The three siblings, aged between eight and 18, were killed around 7.20am after they collided with a lorry travelling in the opposite direction while they were heading from Jalan Parit Haji Omar towards Kayu Ara Pasong on a motorcycle. Pontian police chief Superintendent Hadzrat Hussein Mion Hussain said the pillion riders, aged eight and 11, died at the scene, while the 18-year-old motorcycle rider succumbed to his injuries at Pontian Hospital.

items.title: Ex-prince Andrew search warrants quashed after police accept legal error
items.summary: LONDON: British police on Thursday said that search warrants it secured to search properties linked to King Charles' younger brother Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor had been incorrectly granted and must be quashed. Andrew was suspected of leaking confidential government documents to the late convicted sex-offender Jeffrey Epstein when Andrew was a British trade representative, between 2001 and 2011. Mountbatten-Windsor applied for the search warrants to be quashed and Thames Valley Police said it accepted that they had not been properly granted.

items.title: Trump voters are not pumped about voting in the midterms, poll finds
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Voters who backed Democratic former Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024 are far more enthusiastic about casting ballots this November than those who supported President Donald Trump, a Reuters/Ipsos poll found, in a potential warning sign for Republicans heading into the midterm elections. That could signal erosion in Republican support among a demographic that was a pillar of Trump's 2024 victory. By comparison, just 30 per cent of Trump voters said the same in the poll.

items.title: Tanjong Karang crash: 'Norawalysa was a caring, dedicated' teacher'
items.summary: TANJONG KARANG: A special education teacher who was killed along with her two children in a crash on Jalan Raja Muda Musa here today was described as a dedicated and committed educator. Norawalysa Mat Talpi, 44, a teacher with the Integrated Special Education Programme (PPKI) at SK Bestari Jaya, was remembered by parents and colleagues as a caring teacher who was well-liked at the school. Parent Saridon Ratiman, 58, said his youngest daughter, Nur Afeeya Nayla, eight, was among the last pupils to see Norawalysa before leaving school around noon today.

items.title: [UPDATED] Haze: Putrajaya schools to be closed tomorrow
items.summary: The Putrajaya Education Department said the closure was based on Air Pollutant Index readings as of 5pm today. "All education institutions affected by the closure must implement home-based teaching and learning (PdPR) measures to ensure continuity in students' learning. It said it was continuously monitoring API readings for follow-up action in accordance with Education Ministry guidelines.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Thursday, October 8, 2026

items.title: 'Tonto' claims trial to 55 charges of bribing traffic cops RM62,900
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A 'tonto' (lookout) pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court today to 55 charges of giving RM62,900 in bribes to three traffic police officers between January 2022 and February this year. According to the charges, Ang was alleged to have corruptly given money to three traffic police officers from the Petaling Jaya District Police Headquarters, Negri Sembilan Police Contingent Headquarters and the Kesas Expressway EMPV Patrol Office, as an inducement for them not to inspect lorries during roadblocks. The bribes were allegedly given in several transactions at several bank branches in Klang and Setia Alam, involving amounts ranging from RM700 to RM2,000.

items.title: Schools in Selangor, Melaka to close tomorrow over haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: All schools and educational institutions under the Education Ministry (MoE) in Selangor and Melaka will be closed from tomorrow due to worsening haze. In Selangor, state Education Department director Datin Wan Nor Ashikin Abu Kassim said all educational institutions under the ministry would remain closed until further notice. In Melaka, state Education, Higher Education and Religious Affairs Committee chairman Datuk Rahmad Mariman said all schools under MOE would be closed tomorrow after API readings in key areas of the state exceeded 150.

items.title: Report lodged over sexual AI content involving Kedah students, teachers
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has received a complaint over the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) to create and distribute sexual images and videos involving students and teachers at a school in Kedah. In a statement, MCMC said the misuse of AI to create or distribute sexual content that could affect the safety, dignity and wellbeing of victims, particularly children, is subject to action under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998. MCMC reminded the public not to create, upload or redistribute sexual content involving or allegedly involving children, as such actions could harm victims and affect the investigation process.

items.title: Three siblings killed in Pontian crash buried in single grave [WATCH]
items.summary: PONTIAN: Three siblings killed in a motorcycle-lorry collision in Jalan Parit Haji Sirat here earlier today were buried in a single grave at the Kampung Parit Haji Siraj Muslim cemetery. Nor Daniel Aiman Norlizan, 18, Nor Daniel Fikri, 11, and Puteri Naufa Raisha, 8, were buried at 7.30pm after funeral prayers at Masjid Jamek Kampung Parit Haji Siraj. Fikri and Naufa died at the scene, while Aiman died on the way to Pontian Hospital.

items.title: PH unveils 'Melaka Rumah Kita' concept for state election
items.summary: MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan will introduce the 'Melaka Rumah Kita' concept in the upcoming Melaka polls, with its manifesto and vision for the state to be unveiled during the campaign. PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the concept would outline the coalition's aspirations for Melaka, the livelihood of its people and the direction it intends to take the state if given the mandate. "What is Melaka Rumah Kita?

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 8, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Here are today's biggest stories: Schools closure His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has advised that schools in areas recording prolonged API readings between 150 and 180 be closed amid the worsening haze situation. Indonesia haze response Indonesia has agreed to take the necessary measures to address the worsening haze following discussions between President Prabowo Subianto and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. F1 boosts MSMEs Malaysia's hosting of the Formula 1 Bahrain Grand Prix generated an estimated RM345 million in spillover benefits for MSMEs, highlighting the event's economic impact on local businesses.

items.title: Haze: All schools in Negri Sembilan to close tomorrow
items.summary: SEREMBAN: All educational institutions under the Education Ministry (MoE) in Negri Sembilan will be closed from tomorrow due to the haze affecting the state. The Negri Sembilan Education Department said the closure followed MOE's announcement today , based on the API readings recorded at 5pm at three monitoring stations in Port Dickson, Seremban and Nilai. Earlier, MoE said all educational institutions in areas recording API readings above 180 must be closed from Friday.

items.title: Anwar inspects final preparations for 2027 Budget
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today took time to inspect the final preparations for the delivery of the 2027 Budget at the Finance Ministry. The budget will be tabled by the prime minister, who is also finance minister, in the Dewan Rakyat tomorrow afternoon. One social media user, Ng Ming Lee, hoped that this year's budget would place particular emphasis on welfare and healthcare, while stimulating the country's economy.

items.title: Health Ministry developing index to track food safety controls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry is developing a Food Safety Index to measure the effectiveness of food safety controls across the country's food supply chain. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the index would assess the overall effectiveness of the national food safety control system across three domains, government, industry and consumers. "The initiative is also in line with the National Food Safety Policy 2.0, which strengthens the role of the Food Safety and Quality Programme as the gatekeeper of food safety and reinforces efforts to ensure safe and quality food for the people," he said while winding up the debate on the Food (Amendment) Bill 2026 in the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: Canada's Anne Carson wins Nobel literature prize
items.summary: STOCKHOLM: The Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded on Thursday to Canadian poet Anne Carson, an essayist and classicist who brings a modern twist to mysticism and antiquity in her writings about love, desire and despair. The 76-year-old – who announced in 2024 that she has Parkinson's disease – was honoured "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature," the Swedish Academy said. The permanent secretary of the Academy, Ingrid Carlberg, said she had briefly spoken to Carson.

items.title: AI Nation 2030 push: Ministry of Digital offers 100,000 Coursera licences via Rakyat Digital
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The Ministry of Digital, through MyDigital Corporation, is providing 100,000 learning licences to enable Malaysians to access digital and artificial intelligence (AI) courses through the online learning platform, Coursera. MyDigital Corporation said the initiative forms part of the Rakyat Digital ecosystem and supports the Malaysia Digital 2030 Action Plan (MD2030) and National AI Action Plan 2026-2030, in line with Malaysia’s AI Nation 2030 ambition. Meanwhile, Ministry of Digital Secretary-General Datuk Fabian Bigar said the initiative reflects the ministry’s commitment to making AI and digital learning accessible across all segments of society.

items.title: Schools in Malaysia to close from tomorrow if haze index tops 180, Education Ministry says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Schools and educational institutions under the Education Ministry in areas where the Air Pollutant Index (API) exceeds 180 must close from tomorrow (October 9), as authorities step up measures to protect students and teachers from the worsening haze. Schools in areas where API readings remain above 150 for three consecutive days must also close from Monday, October 12, the ministry said in a statement today. “Areas recording API readings above 150 continuously for three consecutive days must close from Monday, October 12, 2026.”

items.title: Form Two boy injured after alleged beating by Form Four student at Kuala Pilah hostel
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Oct 8 — A Form Two male student was injured after allegedly being beaten by a Form Four student at a secondary school hostel in this district on September 27. Kuala Pilah District Police Chief Supt Muhammad Mustafah Hussin said the incident is believed to have taken place at about 11.40pm in one of the school’s hostels. The victim was then taken to Hospital Tuanku Ampuan Najihah for treatment,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Budget 2027: PM Anwar hopes to strengthen economy, ease rakyat’s burden
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim hopes Budget 2027, to be tabled tomorrow, will further strengthen the national economy while easing the burden on the people. Earlier, Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, inspected the final preparations for the Fifth Madani Budget at the Finance Ministry (MoF) in Putrajaya today ahead of its tabling in the Dewan Rakyat tomorrow. Anwar is scheduled to table Budget 2027 at 3.30pm.

items.title: ‘Ma, I love you… Bye Raa’: Zara Qairina’s tender voice echoes in court as mother breaks down
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 8 — Emotions ran high in the Coroner’s Court here today as the cheerful voice of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir, speaking affectionately to her mother, echoed through the courtroom during the inquest into the Form One student’s death. A total of 42 audio recordings were submitted as evidence, 35 of which captured conversations between Zara Qairina and her mother while the teenager was still alive. Throughout the recordings, Zara Qairina could be heard speaking cheerfully and affectionately as she shared various aspects of her daily life with her mother.

items.title: Budget 2027: Anwar to announce cheaper KTM Southern Shuttle fares, says Loke
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is expected to announce good news regarding an initiative to make the KTM Komuter Southern Shuttle service more affordable during the tabling of the Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat tomorrow. He said that the Southern Shuttle, launched in June, has so far transported approximately 20,000 passengers, averaging between 200 and 300 passengers daily. Loke had previously said that Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) utilises existing trains to operate the Southern Shuttle service, which connects Kulai to Johor Bahru Sentral, as well as Kempas Baru, Pasir Gudang and Paloh.

items.title: Families of 54 Malaysians missing in Nepal floods welcome 45‑day declaration proposal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — A proposal by Nepal to shorten the period for declaring disaster missing persons dead from 12 years to 45 days has brought relief to families of 54 Malaysians still missing after the flood tragedy there. Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (Masfih) welcomed the proposal, describing it as a major relief for the 54 families facing emotional and financial strain 44 days after the tragedy. Masfih spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said all the families hoped the proposed provision could be implemented immediately to provide clarity for the next of kin of Malaysians still missing following the landslide and floods along the Nepal China border on Aug 26.

items.title: ‘Tonto’ pleads not guilty to 55 bribery charges totalling RM62,900 involving traffic police
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 8 — A ‘tonto’ (lookout) pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to 55 charges of giving RM62,900 in bribes to three traffic police officers between January 2022 and February 2026. According to the charges, the man was alleged to have corruptly given money to three traffic police officers from the Petaling Jaya District Police Headquarters, Negeri Sembilan Contingent Police Headquarters and the Kesas Expressway EMPV Patrol Office, as an inducement for them not to inspect lorries during roadblocks. The bribes were allegedly given in several transactions at several bank branches in Klang and Setia Alam, involving amounts ranging from RM700 to RM2,000.

items.title: Malaysia, Myanmar agree ministries must act together on refugee cooperation, says PM Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Malaysia and Myanmar agree that relevant ministries and agencies need to take coordinated and proactive action to advance bilateral cooperation, including efforts to address the issue of Myanmar refugees in Malaysia. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this was emphasised during his meeting and bilateral talks with Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing today. He said following their joint press conference, he and Min Aung Hlaing attended the Malaysia-Myanmar Cooperation Dialogue at Kompleks Seri Perdana, organised by the Institute of Strategic and International Studies (ISIS) Malaysia.

items.title: NRD issues 169,346 new generation MyKads nationwide in three weeks
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 8 — The National Registration Department (NRD) has issued a total of 169,346 New Generation MyKads nationwide between September 17 and October 6. NRD Director-General Datuk Badrul Hisham Alias said the five states recording the highest issuance are the Federal Territories with 20,592 pieces; Johor (18,871); Sarawak (15,777); Sabah (13,711) and Selangor (13,452). Also present was Terengganu NRD Director Awatif Hannan Md Yusup.

items.title: Anthony Loke: RTS Link not delayed, buffer time needed for safety approvals
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 8 — Malaysia and Singapore jointly decided to start the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link operations in February 2027, rather than taking a unilateral step, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said. The minister said the approvals involved Malaysia’s Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) and Singapore’s Land Transport Authority (LTA). He said RTS Link operations could start as early as January, but February was chosen to provide a buffer and ensure safety evaluation and technical approvals proceed smoothly.

items.title: SUV driver fined RM4,000 for tailing Zahid Hamidi’s police convoy on Kesas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — A property agent was fined RM4,000 by the Magistrates’ Court here today after pleading guilty to disobeying a police order by following the convoy escorting Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi yesterday. He subsequently paid the fine. Earlier, a video went viral showing an SUV driver following a police convoy escorting the Deputy Prime Minister from Kajang towards Sunway Medical Centre in Subang Jaya.

items.title: Malaysia must strengthen regional cooperation to ensure stable energy supply, says Akmal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Malaysia has highlighted the need to strengthen regional cooperation to ensure a stable and affordable energy supply, alongside efforts to accelerate the transition to low-carbon energy. In a statement, the Ministry of Economy said that the Azec collaboration complements the implementation of the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR), including energy efficiency, renewable energy, green mobility, infrastructure development, and transition financing. Earlier, Akmal Nasrullah also held a bilateral meeting with Josh Wilson, the Deputy Climate Change and Energy Minister from Australia’s Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water, focusing on energy supply security and gas supply between the two countries.

items.title: Kelantan warns: Dogs without anti‑rabies vaccination tags may be culled
items.summary: BACHOK, Oct 8 — Dogs without vaccination tags or that have not received anti-rabies vaccinations after April each year may be culled by local authorities in Kelantan to curb the risk of rabies transmission. State Local Government, Housing, Health and Environment Committee chairman Hilmi Abdullah said the provision is in line with the Kelantan Anti-rabies Vaccination Order, which requires owners to ensure their pet dogs are vaccinated between January and April every year. “This year, 21 dogs in Bachok have been vaccinated, while samples from another 20 dogs have been taken for rabies testing,” he said.

items.title: Three Pontian siblings killed in motorcycle‑lorry crash after insisting on school despite haze closure
items.summary: PONTIAN, Oct 8 — Unconvinced that the school had been closed due to the haze today, an elder brother eventually gave in to his two younger siblings’ insistence on going to school on a motorcycle, before all three were killed in an accident at Jalan Kampung Parit Haji Siraj, Kayu Ara Pasong, here, this morning. The victims’ mother, Julaiha Munaji, 44, said that her two children, Nor Daniel Fikri Norlizan, 11, and Puteri Naufa Raisha, eight, still wanted to go to Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Parit Sapran, despite being informed that the school had been closed due to the haze. She said that they did not believe that the school had been closed, with one of them even reportedly pleading to go to school, while wearing their school uniform and preparing their schoolwork.

items.title: Steven Sim: Tourism surge and foreign fans drive RM345m SME gains from Bahrain F1 GP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSME) reaped over RM345 million in economic spillover effects of the Bahrain Gulf Air Formula 1 (F1) Grand Prix (GP) at Sepang International Circuit. Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim Chee Keong added that almost half of the 261,000 spectators were foreign tourists. “The impact reflects the important role of large-scale international sporting events in stimulating economic activities, especially through the rise in tourism expenditure and demand for local goods and services.

items.title: Dzulkefly: Food Bill proposes publishing non-compliant food information without court order
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The government has proposed expanding the powers of the Director-General of Health to publish information on food that does not comply with the Food Act 1983 (Act 281) or regulations made under it, without a court order. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the proposal under the Food (Amendment) Bill 2026 would allow such information to be published through print or electronic media in the interest of public safety. He said the 39-clause bill also proposed amendments to Section 12 of Act 281 to allow convictions under the act to be published through print or electronic media.

items.title: AGC objects to former Tabung Haji chairman Abdul Azeez’s bid to challenge IRB over RM4.8m tax settlement
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) has objected to former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim’s application for leave to commence judicial review proceedings against the Inland Revenue Board (IRB), over its alleged unilateral cancellation of an agreement on the settlement of RM4.8 million in tax and penalties. Ng said the impugned letter stated that a review of the case had uncovered new findings and facts concerning income allegedly omitted from the agreement, resulting in the cancellation of the agreement and consequently, the composite assessment with a new tax computation to be issued in due course. “Abdul Azeez was not directed by the impugned letter to pay any additional tax.

items.title: Witness tells court he handed RM350,000 in cash to Hamzah Zainudin’s former aide over PDRM tender
items.summary: Wan Azhar Mohamed Yusof, 51, said he handed over RM100,000 to Sayed Amir Muzzakkir at about 4pm on December 4, 2020, and RM250,000 at 3.30pm on December 16, 2020. The 17th prosecution witness said this when re-examined by Deputy Public Prosecutor Hazel Tan Jia Qi at the trial of Sayed Amir Muzzakkir, who is facing three corruption charges involving RM350,000 in connection with a Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) project tender. Wan Azhar also confirmed that Sayed Amir Muzzakkir had asked him, “Can you pay 350k?

items.title: Why Malaysian professionals look to Singapore? Because many can earn more than double, says HR minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Malaysian professionals could earn significantly higher working in neighbouring Singapore compared to just a median income of around RM6,000 here, according to a study, highlighting a stark wage disparity that Putrajaya is seeking to address through targeted tax incentives and wage growth initiatives. By contrast, a study by government agency TalentCorp showed that a majority of Malaysian professionals employed in Singapore earn between SG$4,001 (RM12,773) and SG$7,000 (RM22,348) per month. Malaysian professionals earning the national median wage of RM6,124 per month are typically subject to a standard personal income tax rate of 19 per cent.

items.title: Jelutong MP urges govt to provide financial assistance to families of Malaysians missing in Nepal floods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The government has been urged to consider providing financial assistance to all Malaysian families whose relatives are still missing due to the floods and landslide disaster in Nepal last August. The matter was proposed by Jelutong Member of Parliament RSN Rayer, who also urged the relevant departments or ministries to consider a moratorium on housing loans, personal bank loans, and vehicle purchases for all victims involved. PHEB Deputy Chairman Senator Dr. R.A. Lingeshwaran said eligible families can apply for the assistance via a QR code displayed on PHEB’s official Facebook account and website.

items.title: E-hailing driver claims trial to driving under influence of drugs, causing Maldivian student’s death on LDP
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 8 — An e-hailing driver today claimed trial in the Magistrate’s Court here to three charges, including causing the death of a Maldivian student in an accident on Sunday. The first charge was framed under Section 44(1)(a) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which carries a maximum prison term of 15 years and a fine of between RM50,000 and RM100,000 upon conviction. The third charge, under Section 43(1) of the act, carries a maximum prison term of 12 months and a fine of between RM5,000 and RM10,000 upon conviction.

items.title: Malaysia needs highly skilled talent to support shift to high-value economy, says Zambry
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 8 — Malaysia needs skilled talent to support its transition to a high-value economy, Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir said. He said the country has several policies and plans to develop highly skilled talent, including the Malaysia Higher Education Blueprint 2026-2035, the 13th Malaysia Plan and the National Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Policy 2030. Zambry said INDEX is more than a platform that brings institutions and industry together; it connects industry needs with the strengths of higher education.

items.title: National Climate Change Bill to institutionalise mandatory carbon accounting, says Arthur Kurup
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The proposed National Climate Change Bill will institutionalise mandatory carbon accounting and clear governance to give businesses the legal certainty needed to decarbonise. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the legislation, alongside the National Climate Change Policy 2.0, would align Malaysia’s environmental agenda with the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR) and New Industrial Master Plan 2030 (NIMP 2030). He said the measure would also strengthen investor confidence and encourage domestic and international investment in clean technologies.

items.title: Anwar personally contacts Indonesian President Prabowo over haze crisis
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today he has personally contacted Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto regarding the “alarming” level of transboundary haze affecting Malaysia and the region. “The matter of the haze is at an alarming level and I’ve personally contacted President Prabowo, and he has agreed to take the necessary steps,” Anwar said. His remarks come as the Department of Environment (DOE) reported that 38 areas in Malaysia recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index readings at 3pm today.

items.title: Selangor govt, state Education Dept to discuss measures to address haze and Super El Nino, says MB
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 8 — Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari will meet the State Education Department (JPNS) tomorrow to discuss follow-up measures regarding the haze situation currently affecting the state. He said the meeting would look into the necessary measures, including those involving school operations, based on developments in air quality and reports from the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) and Department of Environment (DOE). “I will meet JPNS tomorrow to look at what immediate follow-up measures we can take.

items.title: King calls for schools to close if API stays above 150-180 for prolonged period
items.summary: The King expressed concern over the health and safety of schoolchildren and students amid the haze affecting the country, urging the Education Ministry to give serious attention to the situation. “Appropriate measures must be taken by the relevant ministries and agencies to protect schoolchildren and students, including senior citizens and patients with respiratory illnesses. Sultan Ibrahim stressed that the health and safety of schoolchildren and students must be given priority amid the deteriorating air quality.

items.title: Dapat Vista responds to PAC findings, backs urgent completion of formal eJamin agreement
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Dapat Vista (M) Sdn Bhd, the operator of the eJamin court bail payment system, has acknowledged the findings and recommendations of the Public Accounts Committee and supports the urgent completion of a formal agreement with the government. The company, a subsidiary of Pertama Digital Berhad, said the agreement would strengthen accountability and enhance safeguards for bail funds while maintaining continuity of service for the courts and the public. “Public confidence matters to us, and we continue to take our responsibility to bailors seriously,” the companies said.

items.title: Hazy math: DoE explains why your AQI says 250 when the official API is 175
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The Department of Environment (DOE) has clarified that higher air quality figures displayed on independent mobile applications and third-party websites do not reflect data suppression or inaccuracies in official records Just as 38 areas in Malaysia logged unhealthy air quality today, the department explained that Malaysia’s Air Pollutant Index (API) and commercial Air Quality Index (AQI) platforms frequently show divergent numbers because they rely on different index scales, mathematical models, concentration thresholds, averaging durations, update intervals, and sensory inputs. Satellite monitoring, the DOE pointed out, evaluates total aerosol column density across the upper atmosphere rather than air quality at ground level where human respiration occurs. Unhealthy air quality blankets 38 areas As of 3pm today, no monitoring stations in the country recorded good air quality, with 30 stations registering moderate levels and 38 falling into the unhealthy category (API 101 to 200).

items.title: Zambry: MOHE targets 30,000 AI graduates by 2030 to meet future workforce needs
items.summary: Its Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abdul Kadir said the target would be achieved through 30 specialised programmes at bachelor’s, master’s and doctoral (PhD) levels currently offered at 11 public universities. He said to ensure that academic programmes remained relevant to technological advancements, 455 programmes across various levels had undergone a review as of Sept 30. “For specialised AI programmes, development and accreditation have also been strengthened through the Programme Standards: Artificial Intelligence (PS:AI) developed by the Malaysian Qualifications Agency (MQA), to ensure that they are developed systematically and meet the stipulated quality standards,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
